policy_title: Reform Employment Support and Tackle Economic Inactivity
stated: Labour will reform employment support to drive growth and opportunity, underpinned by rights and responsibilities. This includes bringing Jobcentre Plus and the National Careers Service together into a national jobs and careers service. They will support disabled people and those with health conditions into work by tackling Access to Work backlogs and reforming or replacing the Work Capability Assessment. A 'youth guarantee' will provide training, apprenticeships, or support to find work for all 18- to 21-year-olds.

source.quote: Labour will reform employment support so it drives growth and opportunity. Our system will be underpinned by rights and responsibilities – people who can work, should work – and there will be consequences for those who do not fulfil their obligations. We will bring Jobcentre Plus and the National Careers Service together to provide a national jobs and careers service, focused on getting people into work and helping them get on at work. Labour will work with local areas to create plans to support more disabled people and those with health conditions into work. We will tackle the backlog of Access to Work claims and give disabled people the confidence to start working without the fear of an immediate benefit reassessment if it does not work out. We believe the Work Capability Assessment is not working and needs to be reformed or replaced, alongside a proper plan to support disabled people to work. Drawing together existing funding and entitlements, Labour will establish a youth guarantee of access to training, an apprenticeship, or support to find work for all 18- to 21-year-olds, to bring down the number of young people who are not learning or earning. We will also guarantee two weeks’ worth of work experience for every young person, and improve careers advice in schools and colleges.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets employment rate and job access by reforming Jobcentre Plus, tackling economic inactivity, and supporting disabled people and health-condition claimants into work — core O4 indicators.

The youth guarantee and National Careers Service merger explicitly deliver training, apprenticeships, and careers guidance for 18–21 year olds, bearing materially on skills, opportunity, and apprenticeship starts.
Reducing economic inactivity among working-age people (explicitly framed as 'driving growth') would raise aggregate productivity and real living standards through a concrete supply-side mechanism.

Economic inactivity at scale costs the Exchequer via lost income tax/NI receipts and welfare spending; a material reduction would move the debt-path indicator, making fiscal sustainability a non-negligible bearing.

The policy specifically targets groups overrepresented at the bottom of the income distribution (disabled people, young people not in employment/education/training); successful entry into work would directly narrow the income gap.

membership_note: Multi-component policy with distinct programme streams (jobs service, disability/health employment support, youth guarantee), each generating real effects across labour-market quality, skills, growth, fiscal sustainability, and distributional outcomes.
